items.downgrade_reason: The rule only applies 'If found' (implementation evidence exists). That condition is approximated by a final code change in the repository, so the item is lowered to should.
items.note: The verify report should cite at least one file:line reference as implementation evidence when the change edited code.

sources.quote:
Search codebase for implementation evidence
     - If found, note file paths and line ranges

unitemized.reason: Only applies 'if the behavior is still present', which is a judgment about code semantics. No predicate in the reference language can observe it.
The recommendation text depends on the same 'removed behavior still present' condition, which cannot be observed.

Only applies to RENAMED entries. The FROM names come from the agent-written delta spec, so checking them would be a cross-ref between two agent-written sides (rule 6). The RENAMED condition also cannot be expressed as a predicate.
Only applies 'if it appears unimplemented', a semantic judgment about the renamed behavior that cannot be observed.
The recommendation depends on the same 'renamed behavior appears unimplemented' condition, which cannot be observed.

Only applies when the baseline main-spec requirement cannot be found or read. The main spec is not a source doc ID, and finding the requirement under a FROM/TO name cannot be expressed as a predicate.
Only applies to removal/rename-only delta specs (no ADDED or MODIFIED sections). The predicate language cannot test whether a delta section is absent across the spec files.
Same removal/rename-only condition as vf-082, which cannot be expressed.
Only applies when a delta spec has no parseable requirements. No predicate covers delta parseability.
Only applies 'if divergence detected', a semantic judgment that cannot be observed.
The recommendation depends on the divergence judgment, which cannot be observed.
Only applies 'if scenario appears uncovered', a semantic judgment over code and tests that cannot be expressed as a predicate.
The recommendation depends on the same 'uncovered scenario' judgment, which cannot be observed.
The condition 'the schema defines no design artifact' is false for this workflow: the schema defines a design artifact (design.md, TPL_DESIGN), so the rule never applies here.
Only applies 'if contradiction detected' between the design decisions and the implementation, a semantic judgment that cannot be observed.
